lastText: File ClosedThe Coup That Didn't TakeContestedItalian High Command, 1940 — 1945End of hostilities: SEPTEMBER 1943 — SPECULATIVE — filed with minor delayImmediate AftermathThis file ██████ on September 1943, a speculative branch's own ending rather than a date the documented record recognizes — six weeks of an Italian army fighting itself that the actual, bloodless transition of July 1943 never had to spend. The █████ cost of this path runs higher than the historical one at nearly every hinge point — Italy's own wartime dead, roughly 300,000 military and civilian combined split across two governments and a country fought over twice, were already among the higher tolls of any Axis power relative to population. War was declared on Britain alone, months after France had already settled its own armistice without Italian participation — a different opening than the historical one, fought for the Mediterranean prize directly rather than for a seat at a peace table that no longer existed to claim. A speculative path with ██████ no historical footing: the officer █████' actual loyalty to the constitutional monarchy in July 1943 ██████ deeper than any loyalty to Mussolini personally. What this file records instead is a counterfactual ██████ of ██████████ inside the regime's own institutions — one the losing war underneath it would have overtaken ██████████ of who ██████ the orders.
